The method `org.apache.commons.lang.WordUtils.abbreviate` is responsible for abbreviating a given string based on specified indices. The method adjusts the `upper` and `lower` indices based on the length of the input string. If `lower` is greater than the length of the string, it is set to the length of the string. However, the `lower` index is never adjusted to the length of the string. This can lead to issues where `lower` is greater than the length of the string, causing `upper` to also be set incorrectly and leading to `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when trying to substring the string.

The step-by-step diagnosis of the bug is as follows:
1. The `WordUtils.abbreviate` method adjusts the `upper` index to the length of the input string when `upper` is -1 or greater than the length of the string.
2. However, the `lower` index is not adjusted to the length of the string if it is greater than the length of the string.
3. When `lower` is greater than the length of the string, it leads to incorrect adjustment of `upper`, resulting in it also being greater than the length of the string.
4. Subsequently, when trying to substring the string using the incorrect `upper` index, a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` occurs.

To fix this issue, the `lower` index should also be adjusted to the length of the string if it is greater than the length of the string.

Next, I will provide the methods that need to be fixed to address this issue.
The bug can be fixed by adjusting the lower index to the length of the string when it is greater than the length of the string. 

Methods to be fixed:
```
org.apache.commons.lang.WordUtils.abbreviate(java.lang.String,int,int,java.lang.String)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
